name: Ironpass DeepStrata Tunneling Suit Pro
description:
Gunmetal grey reinforced with rust-orange abrasion panels across the knees, elbows, and shoulder caps. The DeepStrata is a purpose-built tunneling suit for underground excavation in GLMZ's subsurface infrastructure corridors — where collapses, gas pockets, and groundwater intrusion are occupational hazards rather than emergencies. Shell is ripstop ballistic nylon over a crushproof foam chassis at impact zones.

Integrated kneepads are gel-filled with a hard outer cap. The collar accepts a standard tunnel respirator bayonet mount. Spinal channel runs full-length up the back, accommodating spinal rigs and exoskeletal harness attachments. Pockets are sealed with magnetic closures rated for dust ingress.
functionality: Impact protection at knees, elbows, and shoulders; spinal channel accommodates spinal rigs and exoskeletal harness mounts; collar bayonet mount accepts standard tunnel respirators; magnetic-seal pockets rated IP65 for dust; reinforced seat panel for confined-space crawl work.
what_it_says: You work below the city where no one is watching and everything can go wrong.
story_hooks: A tunnel crew breaks through a sealed pre-collapse corridor and finds it occupied — someone has been living in the deep grid for years, and they've built something down there.
The spinal channel was spec'd to accommodate standard rigs, but a new military-grade spinal augment doesn't fit — its owner needs a modified suit before the next shift or can't work.
A tunnel worker's suit data-logger — used for safety compliance — has been recording audio; a labor organizer wants the files before the corponation's safety inspector does.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: Heavy-duty utilitarian suit with pronounced angular silhouette. Gunmetal grey dominates the torso and limbs, with rust-orange accent panels creating a high-visibility safety pattern across impact zones. Broad shoulders and reinforced geometry give the wearer an imposing, built-for-punishment appearance. Reads as serious working equipment, not fashion.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with articulated panels for mobility. Tapered slightly at wrists and ankles for seal compatibility. Ample room for layering thermal underlayers. Compression zones at knees and elbows from integrated padding. Designed for function over form.
physical_description.primary_material: Ripstop ballistic nylon shell over crushproof foam impact chassis. High abrasion resistance at stress points.
physical_description.texture: Tight weave ballistic nylon with visible ribbing from underlying foam structure. Impact panels have a slightly softer, spongy tactile quality visible as subtle quilting. Worn areas show characteristic pilling and thread fray from rock contact.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey base with rust-orange abrasion panels at knees, elbows, and shoulder caps. High-contrast safety coloring for underground visibility. Minimal branding in muted grey.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic closures on all sealed pockets. Full front two-way zipper (gunmetal) with storm flap. Reinforced velcro straps at wrists and ankles for seal integrity.
distinctive_features: Integrated gel-filled kneepads with hard outer caps
Full-length dorsal spinal channel for exoskeletal rig attachment
Standard tunnel respirator bayonet mount collar
Sealed magnetic pockets rated for dust ingress
Visible impact foam quilting at high-stress zones
Wear-resistant corner reinforcement at hip pockets
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 working-class professional equipment. Genuine industrial safety suit, not corporate luxury or salvage piece.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by tunnel engineers, subsurface infrastructure crews, and GLMZ excavation teams. Signals honest labor in dangerous conditions—subterranean work, structural risk tolerance, technical competence. Wearer is part of the unglamorous backbone keeping the GLMZ infrastructure functional.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in with visible wear at knees and elbow contact points. Dust coating in crevices. Possible small tears in the ballistic nylon that have been field-patched with synthetic adhesive tape. Magnetic closures may show minor corrosion from sweat and mineral dust. Overall weathered but maintained—this is expensive equipment.
